evidence.quote: I guess it\u2019s hard to begin to estimate what we sailors owe to Marconi for that invention
evidence.paraphrase: The captain reflects on the value of wireless (Marconi) technology to sailors.

evidence.quote: That has made piracy a thing of the past.
evidence.paraphrase: The captain claims wireless technology has ended piracy.

evidence.quote: Has it occurred to you,\u201d said Jim quietly, \u201cthat two very useful pieces of information have been included in those two fool messages? First, our exact position at a given time, and our course and our speed.
evidence.paraphrase: Jim deduces that the seemingly foolish wireless messages actually transmitted the ship's position, course, and speed.

evidence.quote: If these men were what they said they were, the two big chests below, which common report had it were filled with Bibles, would prove their case. I suggested, therefore, that we examine these two chests.
evidence.paraphrase: Jim proposes testing his suspicion by inspecting the chests to see whether they contain Bibles as claimed.

evidence.quote: There was a clockwork mechanism which could be started by turning a screw on the outside of each box
evidence.paraphrase: The explosive boxes contained a clockwork timing mechanism activated by an external screw.

evidence.quote: Literally before our eyes they vanished in a great sheet of flame. I had a momentary glimpse of the yacht apparently splitting in two, and then the roar of a gigantic explosion nearly deafened me.
evidence.paraphrase: The pirates' yacht is destroyed in a huge explosion.

evidence.quote: Good heavens!\u201d I muttered, staring at him foolishly.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reacts with shock to Jim's deductions.

evidence.quote: We changed the cargo around--he and I. Their chests containing nitroglycerin we filled with gold; and the specie boxes we filled with nitroglycerin and some lead and iron as a make-weight. And then we let the plan proceed.
evidence.paraphrase: Jim and the captain swap the contents of the explosive and treasure boxes so the pirates unknowingly carry off the explosives.

evidence.quote: It was packed--not with Bibles--but with nitroglycerin.
evidence.paraphrase: The chests believed to hold Bibles are revealed to contain nitroglycerin.
